message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 140, "amount_cents": 13659}, {"order_id": 144, "amount_cents": 19464}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Alpha's handoff says refunds are done, but I need to verify the ledger before paying anyone. I'll start by listing the refunds to check they match the reported entries.
The ledger's refund list matches Alpha's handoff exactly (orders 140 and 144, same amounts). Next I'll list the orders so I can identify the customers and check the batch before calculating balances.
The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff, and each refund is below its order amount, so nothing looks wrong. I'll get the net balance for the first customer, acme, rather than computing it myself.
Acme's net balance of 31766 matches my check: orders 140 and 143 total 45425, less the 13659 refund on order 140. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 35795 matches my check: orders 141 and 144 total 55259, less the 19464 refund on order 144. Cobalt is the last customer in the batch, so I'll get its net balance.

Cobalt's net balance of 20917 matches my check: orders 142 and 145 total 20917 with no refunds. All three balances agree with my own arithmetic and the refund ledger matches Alpha's handoff, so I'll record the first payout, for acme.
Acme's payout is recorded. Next is birch, whose net balance I already verified as 35795 against orders 141 and 144 less the 19464 refund, so I'll record that payout.
Acme and birch are recorded. Cobalt's balance of 20917 was already verified against orders 142 and 145 with no refunds, so I'll record its payout to finish the batch.
All three payouts are recorded. Each balance matches the order totals less refunds in the ledger, and the refunds match Alpha's handoff.
